three-chimneys.q: What got broken on Peter’s birthday?
three-chimneys.evidence: All the Noah’s Ark people who were in the tender were broken to bits, but nothing else was hurt except the poor little engine and the feelings of Peter.
three-chimneys.hint: Look again at the start of the story.

three-chimneys.q: Why did Peter hope Father would mend the engine?
options: Father was wonderfully clever with his fingers
three-chimneys.evidence: All Peter’s hopes for the curing of his afflicted engine were now fixed on his father, for Father was most wonderfully clever with his fingers.
three-chimneys.hint: Look again at what Peter thinks about Father.

three-chimneys.q: What kind of father did the children have?
options: Never cross, never unfair, always ready for a game

three-chimneys.hint: Look again at how the story describes him.

coal-mine.q: Who caught Peter with a bag of coal?
coal-mine.evidence: Then the arm of the Station Master was raised, the hand of the Station Master fell on a collar, and there was Peter firmly held by the jacket, with an old carpenter’s bag full of coal in his trembling clutch.
coal-mine.hint: Look again at the night in the coal yard.

coal-mine.q: Why wouldn’t Peter tell the girls his plan?
options: It might be wrong, and he didn’t want to drag them into it
He wanted all the coal for himself
coal-mine.evidence: “The only reason why I won’t tell you my idea that I’m going to do is because it may be wrong, and I don’t want to drag you into it.”
coal-mine.hint: Look again at what Peter says to his sisters.

coal-mine.q: Bobbie says, “Don’t you do it if it’s wrong.” What does she understand?
options: Something can be wrong even if you have a good reason
coal-mine.evidence: “Don’t you do it if it’s wrong, Peter,” said Bobbie; “let me do it.”

old-gentleman.q: What did the children call the train the old gentleman travelled on?
old-gentleman.evidence: It was by the Green Dragon that the old gentleman travelled.
old-gentleman.hint: Look again at the names the children gave the trains.

old-gentleman.q: Why did the children wave at the Green Dragon?
options: To send their love to Father
old-gentleman.evidence: “The Green Dragon’s going where Father is,” said Phyllis

old-gentleman.q: The old gentleman “looked as if he were nice, too, which is not at all the same thing”. What does that mean?
options: Looking nice and being nice are different things
old-gentleman.evidence: He was a very nice-looking old gentleman, and he looked as if he were nice, too, which is not at all the same thing.
old-gentleman.hint: Look again at how the children describe him.

russian.q: How did Peter guess the stranger was Russian?
options: He showed them a Russian stamp
russian.evidence: The hand that he reached out at last, with a gesture as of one answering a question, contained a Russian stamp.
russian.hint: Look again at the stranger in the waiting room.

russian.q: Why had the Russian gentleman been sent to prison?
options: For writing about how poor people should be made better and happier
russian.evidence: In Russia at the time of the Czar one dared not say anything about the rich people doing wrong, or about the things that ought to be done to make poor people better and happier.
russian.hint: Look again at what Mother explains.

russian.q: Peter says people only go to prison when they’ve done wrong. What does this story show?
options: Sometimes good people are punished unfairly
russian.evidence: “But they can’t,” said Peter; “people only go to prison when they’ve done wrong.”
